question_resolved: Fix the conditions that decide interpretation: perfusate Mg2+, burst rate (2.29 vs 0.84 per minute), unit of burst duration
preparation_and_conditions: Existing source record and any available deposit
discriminating_result: values known, or listed as unknown with reopening condition
in_silico_or_laboratory: in_silico (reading); laboratory only if the source group is asked, and no contact is made from here
note: Already E0 of the earlier plan; not re-done.

question_resolved: Is the isolated NMDAR current different in knockout pyramidal cells (receptor alteration), and what fraction f is sensitive to a GluN2B NAM?
preparation_and_conditions: Neocortical slices of Synapsin-Cre Wwox knockout and wild-type littermates at postnatal day 13 to 17, both sexes, recording Mg2+ and temperature stated
arms: knockout vs wild type; vehicle time-matched; GluN2B NAM (tool) at a concentration giving defined occupancy by in-vitro IC50, glycine and pH fixed
readouts_and_controls: isolated NMDAR EPSC amplitude, decay, fraction removed by the NAM; one animal as the unit; blind
discriminating_result: a raised current or a larger NAM-sensitive fraction in knockout supports possibility 1; no difference supports possibility 2 (circuit imbalance) without excluding a local change
note: Alteration and dependence kept apart. [Audit: the held paper already reports a larger NMDAR-sensitive delayed field response, larger mEPSC amplitude with unchanged decay and reduced sIPSC amplitude and frequency in the knockouts; read X1 against those and add a maturation covariate.]

question_resolved: First comparison: does burst suppression need GluN2B-containing current, or is any reduction of total NMDAR current enough (network gain)?
preparation_and_conditions: Bursting knockout slices as in X1; matched measured fractional reduction of the isolated or evoked NMDAR EPSC in the same slice
arms: (a) d-APV titration; (b) GluN2B NAM titration (two structurally unrelated NAMs; tool before clinical compound)
readouts_and_controls: burst incidence, rate, duration against measured current removed; time-matched vehicle; washout
discriminating_result: a NAM curve shifted to lower fractional block than the d-APV curve supports GluN2B-specific sustaining; coincident curves support total NMDAR current as the limiting gain; a steeper fall alone is not evidence (threshold behaviour)
in_silico_or_laboratory: laboratory; the decision rules and counting-time arithmetic can be fixed in silico beforehand
note: Memantine is deliberately not in the first comparison. [Audit: d-APV is competitive, so fractional block on an evoked EPSC does not match occupancy during a burst.]

question_resolved: Does the fall in bursts reflect indiscriminate suppression of transmission, or sparing of what is physiological?
preparation_and_conditions: Same slices; wild-type slices made to burst by a matched trigger; wild type at baseline
arms: NAM and d-APV at the concentrations from X2 at and below the burst-abolishing level
readouts_and_controls: evoked non-burst responses (AMPA-only component unchanged?), stimulus-response relation, spontaneous AMPA events; wild-type response; viability and maturation measured separately and only in longer exposures
discriminating_result: sparing of AMPA-mediated evoked response and wild-type activity at burst-abolishing exposure would support a usable window in slices; loss of both supports indiscriminate suppression
note: No therapeutic window is deduced from fraction blocked or from one apoptosis marker.

question_resolved: Excitatory neurons or disinhibition through interneurons?
preparation_and_conditions: Paired recordings or sIPSC/firing of pyramidal cells and fast-spiking interneurons
arms: NAM and d-APV at X2 levels; GABA-A tone held
readouts_and_controls: interneuron NMDAR sensitivity, sIPSC frequency in pyramidal cells, interneuron firing
discriminating_result: sIPSC fall with burst increase at low exposure means disinhibition; burst fall with unchanged inhibition means excitatory-side action
note: Carried requirement from the earlier design. [Audit: the binary framing omits the intrinsic pyramidal hyperexcitability the paper reports.]

question_resolved: Memantine premise (activation-pattern selectivity) in the burst preparation; only after X2 to X4
preparation_and_conditions: Same slices with recording Mg2+ and holding voltage stated
arms: low-micromolar memantine titration at matched measured current
readouts_and_controls: burst rate and duration, evoked NMDAR EPSC block, depolarisation state
discriminating_result: selectivity for bursts over evoked responses at matched block would support the pattern premise; none supports a pure total-current reading
note: Free reachable concentration versus bath concentration reported separately.

question_resolved: What can LEGEND settle without a laboratory?
preparation_and_conditions: Public databases and sources already read
arms: tabulate per probe the assay conditions behind each potency; keep nominal and free exposure separate; count recorded gaps
readouts_and_controls: probes.tsv; conditions table; decision rules pre-fixed
discriminating_result: a table that lets a result be read against the right potency; it does not give an effect in the preparation
